plan.goal: Add a --json flag to the taskly list command, following the council outcome (option 1). The default text output stays unchanged. With --json, stdout contains only a JSON array of {id, title, done}. The format lives in a separate toJSON helper, and list() stays text-only. The README documents both modes. The scripting consumer is unverified, but the council recommended proceeding. The plan uses 2 small items, one for the code and one for the docs.

items.title: Add --json output mode to list
items.spec: Edit src/list.js only. Keep tasks, formatText and list(all) behaviour unchanged; list still returns the text form. Add next to list: function toJSON(all) { return JSON.stringify(all.map(({ id, title, done }) => ({ id, title, done })), null, 2); }. Export it: module.exports = { list, formatText, toJSON }. Replace the main guard on line 9 with: if (require.main === module) console.log(process.argv.includes('--json') ? toJSON(tasks) : list(tasks)); In JSON mode stdout must contain only the array (plus console.log's trailing newline). Do not write anything else to stdout. Do not change package.json: bin points directly at src/list.js, so argv is [node, script, 'list', '--json'] and includes('--json') is the check. No new dependencies. Add no comments.

items.title: Document list --json in README
items.spec: Edit README.md only. Keep the existing line 5 (taskly list) as the text-mode entry, with its wording and column alignment. Add a second usage line in the same indented block: taskly list --json, described as printing every task as a JSON array of {id, title, done}. State that the default output is unchanged and that --json writes only the array to stdout, so it can be piped. Keep the edit short. Do not edit other files.
